name: push-tag-human-approved-release-only
body:
The recurring release law: push and tag are human-approved acts. The law carries one name on every surface that states it — the agent-policy surfaces (`opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`), the binary-doc surfaces (`Cargo.toml`, `src/git/mod.rs`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs`, `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs` in `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at`, `tests/git_e2e.rs`, `tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`), and the user-doc surface (`README.md`). `README.md` and `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs` state "push/tag remain human-approved". The wording carries the law; the binary's git2-only behaviour (`default-features = false`; the git CLI stays unshelled) and `scripts/release.sh`'s behaviour of leaving pushing to humans hold. `plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md` is a historical plan record and stays outside this requirement.

WHO PUSHES/TAGS, AND HOW. Only the optional per-repo `release-agent` (see `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent`) holds `git push`/`git tag`, and its grant is `ask`: every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. The `codebase-navigator` additionally captures explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching it via `task`, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command. Every OTHER generated agent — the core/root `implementer`, each per-subsystem `<name>-implementer`, and each tiered `test-implementer` — holds zero push/tag grant: under the deny-by-default permission block the verbs are absent, hence denied. The template scaffolds push/tag `ask` on the optional release-agent alone, and its git-conventions interview reserves push/tag for that agent.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every listed surface states the rule as "human-approved acts" (or, for a sentence about the release-agent, states the release-agent-only + `ask` model).
- `README.md` and the `apg plan verify` merge-handoff string in `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at` state "push/tag remain human-approved".
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` grants `git push`/`git tag` ONLY to the optional `release-agent`, and only as `ask`; its permission-shape prose, its git-conventions interview, and its permission-value prose carry zero instruction to scaffold push/tag `ask` on every generated agent and zero offer of push/tag as a per-agent choice.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` states the navigator obtains explicit user consent before dispatching the release-agent, and its push/tag clause says human-approved.
- `AGENTS.md` states push/tag are human-approved acts and that only the release-agent may push/tag (behind the consent gate and the per-op `ask`).
- The binary's git2-only behaviour and `scripts/release.sh`'s behaviour of leaving pushing to humans hold.
- `plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md` stays outside this requirement (historical).
- Scope is product source + the repo guide + the named binary-doc/test surfaces plus `README.md` and `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and stay outside this requirement.
